name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of roughly D+22
Open seat after Frederica Wilson's retirement, removing incumbent advantage
Heavy outside spending opposing Gilbert but no polling to confirm impact
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near certain to win
model.rationale: The seat's deep Democratic lean and Polymarket pricing near 96% for the Democrat make this Safe D despite the open seat and significant outside opposition spending against Gilbert. With no polls available, the fundamentals carry the forecast, trimmed slightly for the incumbent's absence.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the Republican nominee closing within single digits, or a scandal involving Gilbert, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This Miami-area seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Florida, and Frederica Wilson's retirement does not change the underlying partisan balance. Oliver Gilbert has outraised his Republican rival and benefits from name recognition as a local official, though outside groups have spent heavily opposing him.

Te Mayonna Brown faces an uphill battle in a district where the Democratic baseline advantage exceeds twenty points. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee at roughly 96 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast treats this as Safe D, with modest uncertainty from the open-seat dynamic and the absence of polling.
